t: Hinduism has no single founder or creed: it grew from the Vedic religion of the north-west of India and absorbed many local traditions over three thousand years.
Its central ideas, dharma, karma, rebirth and release (moksha), and its devotion to gods such as Vishnu, Shiva and the Goddess shaped the culture of South Asia and much of Southeast Asia.
Reformed and renewed in the 19th and 20th centuries, it is the world’s third-largest religion, with about 1.2 billion followers and communities on every continent.
dyk: Angkor Wat in Cambodia, often called the largest religious monument in the world, was built in the early 12th century as a temple to Vishnu.
ev: The hymns of the Rigveda, the oldest Hindu scripture, are composed in north-west India
The earliest Upanishads explore the identity of the self (atman) and ultimate reality (Brahman)
The Mahabharata, with the Bhagavad Gita, and the Ramayana take shape
Under the Gupta Empire, temple building, the Puranas and devotion to Vishnu and Shiva flourish
Shankara teaches Advaita Vedanta, the non-dual reading of the Upanishads
Angkor Wat is built as a temple to Vishnu under the Khmer king Suryavarman II
Swami Vivekananda introduces Hinduism to the World’s Parliament of Religions in Chicago
The constitution of the Republic of India abolishes untouchability

f.origin: The Indian subcontinent: the Vedic religion of the north-west from about 1500 BCE, with older and local traditions
f.founder: None: its teachings are traced to the seers of the Vedas and a long line of sages and teachers
f.scriptures: The Vedas and Upanishads; the epics Mahabharata (with the Bhagavad Gita) and Ramayana; the Puranas
f.followers: About 1.2 billion (2020), most of them in India and Nepal
